physical.viewerQuestion: Why does this weighted toy return upright after a small tilt?
physical.likelyIntuition: A viewer may expect a tipped object to stay tipped or fall over.
physical.missingInsight: For this toy, tilting raises its centre of mass; returning upright lowers gravitational potential energy.
physical.openingDemonstration: Show the same toy tilted slightly and released, then reveal the low internal weight while repeating the motion.

causalSteps.cause: Tilt this curved-base toy slightly away from its upright position.
causalSteps.effect: Its centre of mass rises, and gravity creates a restoring turning effect for the illustrated configuration.
causalSteps.visual: Track the centre of mass and its height while the curved base rolls; show the force and contact point.

physical.takeaway: Predict return or further tipping by how a small tilt changes the centre-of-mass height.

transferTest.question: Would moving the internal weight upward necessarily preserve the same stability?
transferTest.expectedAnswer: No. The resulting centre-of-mass path can change, so the geometry and weight placement must be checked again.

physical.scopeBoundary: Explain the small-tilt response of the illustrated toy, not all shapes or every possible tilt.
assumptions: The illustrated base and weight placement make upright a local minimum of centre-of-mass height.

maths.viewerQuestion: Why can you add the same number to both sides of an equation?
maths.likelyIntuition: A learner may know a symbol-moving rule without understanding why equality survives.
maths.missingInsight: Adding equal amounts preserves the zero difference between equal quantities.
maths.openingDemonstration: Show two equal quantities moving together along paired number lines, then contrast changing only one side.

causalSteps.cause: Add three to each side of a true equality between real numbers.
causalSteps.effect: Both values increase equally, so the difference between them remains zero.
causalSteps.visual: Move equal marked positions three units together and display their unchanged difference.

maths.takeaway: Explain why adding the same amount preserves equality and identify when an unequal change breaks it.

transferTest.question: Starting from equal quantities, what happens if you add three to only one side?
transferTest.expectedAnswer: The changed side exceeds the other by three, so that equality no longer holds.

maths.scopeBoundary: Explain addition preserving equality; leave multiplication, division and inequalities for later.
assumptions: The quantities are real numbers and the same number is added to both sides.
